transcript.text: Samsung WD90T534DBW washer dryer - clothes are still damp at the end of the wash and dry programme. It's not that old. Is the heater going?

In fact, on a washer-dryer, the most common reasons for damp clothes are either that the load was too large for the drying cycle (a dryer holds significantly less than a washer), or that airflow is restricted by a blocked lint filter or condenser. 1. Load size: Was the drum more than half full? If so, try drying a smaller load next time.
2. Lint filter: Located at the bottom front behind a small flap, this needs to be clean for air to circulate and heat effectively. If you confirm the load was small (e.g., 3-4kg) and the filter is clean, we can then look deeper into whether the heater element or its safety thermostat has failed.
I load a full 9kg drum and wash and dry in one go. The manual says 6kg for drying though. Haven't checked the filter yet, but there are no error codes and the drum gets hot.

The dampness is probably because you are drying a 9kg load when the machine's dry capacity is only 6kg; trying to dry more than half the wash load will leave clothes wet regardless of how well it works. However, because restricted airflow can also cause this even with heat present, please unplug the machine and check the lint filter at the bottom front. Is it clean?
I haven't checked the filter yet, I'll have a look. Would a half load with full spin be worth trying too?

Yes, absolutely. Drying a 6kg load that has been spun as high as possible is much more effective than trying to dry 9kg. However, even with a smaller load, the machine needs good airflow to work properly. Please unplug it and check the lint filter in the door opening and the condenser unit behind the bottom flap—are they clean?
I'll check the filter and condenser now. Haven't looked yet, so I'll report back. A half load did come out dry when I tried it with full spin, by the way.

That suggests it is simply an overloading issue. A washer-dryer has a much smaller drying capacity than washing capacity; putting 9kg of wet clothes into a machine rated for only 6kg means the dryer cannot circulate enough hot air to evaporate all that moisture, even if the drum gets hot. The fix is straightforward: always separate your laundry. This will give you dry clothes every time without needing any repairs.

claimsRejected.claim: To answer your question directly: wet clothes do not automatically mean the heater has failed.

Faulty drying heater or thermal cut-out (low)
